$description: Canadian corporate income tax rates for 2026: federal and provincial/territorial general and small-business (CCPC) rates on active business income. Rates are decimals.

federal.note: General rate is 38% less 10% federal abatement less 13% general rate reduction = 15%. The small-business rate applies to CCPC active business income up to the business limit, shared among associated corporations and phased out at high taxable capital.

SK.name: Saskatchewan
SK.note: Saskatchewan's 1% small-business rate was made permanent in 2025; its business limit is $600,000, the only province above $500,000.

ON.name: Ontario
ON.note: Small-business rate reduced from 3.2% to 2.2% for taxation years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.

QC.name: Quebec
QC.note: Small-business rate reduced from 3.2% to 2.2% for taxation years beginning after April 29, 2026. Quebec's small-business rate requires minimum employee paid-hours; corporations that do not qualify pay the general rate.

NS.name: Nova Scotia
NS.note: General rate cut from 16% to 14% and small-business rate from 2.5% to 1.5% effective April 1, 2025.

NL.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
NL.note: Small-business rate reduced from 2.5% to 2.0% effective January 1, 2026.

notes: Rates shown are calendar-2026 statutory rates; mid-year changes (ON and QC small-business cuts) apply by taxation-year start date and are noted per jurisdiction.
CCPC investment income is taxed federally at 38.67% (with refundable components) — not modelled here.
Verify against the relevant provincial finance department before filing; provincial budgets can change rates in-year.
